topics.mining: Use any pickaxe to collect concrete. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing. Silk Touch is unnecessary, and Fortune does not increase the drop.
topics.location: Make concrete by bringing concrete powder of the desired color into contact with source or flowing water.
topics.fire: Concrete does not catch fire or burn away.
topics.gravity: Concrete stays in place without support; it does not fall like concrete powder.
topics.water: Concrete stays concrete in water. To make it, harden concrete powder with source or flowing water.

topics.mining: Concrete powder drops itself when broken by hand or with a tool; a shovel is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary and Fortune does not increase the drop.
topics.location: Craft concrete powder from sand, gravel and the desired dye. It is a manufactured building material.
topics.fire: Concrete powder does not catch fire or burn away.
topics.gravity: Concrete powder falls when unsupported. Falling powder can bury and suffocate you. Keep support under it when building.
topics.water: Source or flowing water hardens concrete powder into concrete of the same color. Rain and splash water bottles do not harden it.

topics.mining: Wool drops itself when broken by hand or with a tool. Shears are fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary and Fortune does not increase the block drop.
topics.location: Shear an adult sheep of the desired color to get wool, or use the matching dye in wool recipes. You can craft white wool from string.
topics.fire: Wool is flammable and can burn away. Keep it away from fire and lava.
topics.gravity: Wool stays in place without support; it does not fall.
topics.water: Wool does not dissolve or change color in water. It cannot be waterlogged.

topics.mining: Use a Silk Touch tool to collect this glass block. Without Silk Touch it drops nothing. Fortune does not help recover it.
topics.location: Smelt sand or red sand into glass. Use dye with glass to make stained glass in the desired color.
topics.fire: Glass does not catch fire or burn away.
topics.gravity: Glass stays in place without support; it does not fall.
topics.water: Full glass blocks cannot be waterlogged. They can be used as walls to hold back water.

topics.mining: Use a Silk Touch tool to collect glass panes. Without Silk Touch they drop nothing. Fortune does not help recover them.
topics.location: Craft glass panes from glass blocks, or stained glass panes from matching stained glass. Some buildings also contain panes.
topics.fire: Glass panes do not catch fire or burn away.
topics.gravity: Glass panes stay in place without support; they do not fall.
topics.water: Glass panes can be waterlogged, so water can occupy the same block space as a pane.

topics.mining: Tinted glass drops itself even when broken by hand. Silk Touch is unnecessary, and Fortune does not increase the drop.
topics.location: Craft tinted glass from glass and amethyst shards. It blocks light while still letting you see through it.
topics.fire: Tinted glass does not catch fire or burn away.
topics.gravity: Tinted glass stays in place without support; it does not fall.
topics.water: Tinted glass cannot be waterlogged. It can hold water back as a full block.

topics.mining: Logs drop themselves when broken by hand or with a tool; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary, and Fortune does not increase the drop.
topics.location: Get logs by chopping the matching tree. Grow more of that tree using its appropriate sapling or propagule. Stripped logs are made by using an axe on a log.
topics.fire: These Overworld logs are flammable and can burn away. Stripping them does not make them fireproof.
topics.gravity: Logs stay in place without support; they do not fall.
topics.stripping: Use an axe on an unstripped log to remove its bark. This changes the block into its stripped version; it does not drop the bark as an item.

topics.mining: Wood blocks drop themselves when broken by hand or with a tool; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary, and Fortune does not increase the drop.
topics.location: Craft all-bark wood from matching logs. Use an axe on unstripped wood to make the stripped form.
topics.fire: These Overworld wood blocks are flammable. Stripping them does not make them fireproof.
topics.gravity: Wood blocks stay in place without support; they do not fall.
topics.stripping: Use an axe on unstripped wood to change it into stripped wood. Already stripped wood cannot be stripped a second time.

topics.mining: Stems and hyphae drop themselves when broken by hand or with a tool; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary, and Fortune does not increase the drop.
topics.location: Harvest crimson or warped stems from the matching huge fungus in the Nether, or grow huge fungi. Craft hyphae from matching stems; use an axe for stripped forms.
topics.fire: Crimson and warped stems and hyphae do not catch fire or burn away. Their dropped items can still be destroyed in fire or lava.
topics.gravity: Stems and hyphae stay in place without support; they do not fall.
topics.stripping: Use an axe on an unstripped stem or hyphae block to make its stripped form. Already stripped forms cannot be stripped again.

topics.mining: Planks drop themselves when broken by hand or with a tool; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary, and Fortune does not increase the drop.
topics.location: Craft matching planks from the corresponding logs or wood. Bamboo planks are made from bamboo blocks instead.
topics.fire: Overworld and bamboo planks are flammable and can burn away. Keep them away from fire and lava.
topics.gravity: Planks stay in place without support; they do not fall.

topics.mining: Planks drop themselves when broken by hand or with a tool; an axe is fastest. Silk Touch is unnecessary, and Fortune does not increase the drop.
topics.location: Craft crimson or warped planks from the matching stems or hyphae.
topics.fire: Crimson and warped planks do not catch fire or burn away. Their dropped items can still be destroyed in fire or lava.
topics.gravity: Planks stay in place without support; they do not fall.
